transcript.text: Good evening, everyone. 07:00, time to commence this hearing of the Inland Wetlands and Water Courses Commission. The objective of the hearing is to obtain information and hear public comments regarding IWWC 2,036 applications to construct a wetland crossing for proposed driveway and new construction. In keeping with the usual procedures of the Commission in the hearing, I will ask in order first for the applicants or their agent to comment on the proposal with special reference to how the plans have been modified or evolved in response to comments at previous meetings. I'll afford an opportunity for commissioners to inquire, ask questions about the proposed permit, and finally, I'll open the hearing to public comment from interested parties. I see on screen that we have Commissioner Larson, Commissioner Hallisey, alternate Monroe, of course myself, Acting Chairman George Eliot present for the meeting. We will seat Mr. Monroe for the hearing and for the subsequent meeting that will follow. I was informed that Commissioner Lowy would not be able to attend, and evidently Commissioner Smith also. Okay. So, proceeding then to Item three of the hearing agenda, I will ask the applicants again or their agent as preferred

to again briefly outline the proposal and especially focus on the modifications, recent modifications. Note that we have in our record online a new crossing plan dated threeonetwenty one and a construction sequence final draft to reference for the application. So I'll turn it over to the applicants. Who wants to speak?

Then I'll ask George Logan, who is also on the call, to please feel free to follow-up here after I do my best here to describe the application. So what's being proposed is a crossing of a wetlands of two wetlands areas. They actually, we believe they're intermittent streams, during the wet season. There can be some, you know, a few inches of water that'll collect, especially, after a good rain, event happens. proposal involves us, sort of following the grade of the area right off of Pine Ridge Road, and then as you know, if you live in the area, particularly on that side of Pine Ridge, it dips down, there's a corridor where these, wetlands areas, go through. Once we get down, once you get down into the low lying area, the plan involves raising the crossing up approximately five or six feet, and we would have interlocking concrete blocks to kind of create the outer walls and then fill the interior portion of it, and put a gravel driveway on top of it. The two streams that go underneath this crossing, would flow through
